headline: Highest risk is medium: Firecrawl’s broad network egress can leak or misroute content into a non-networked documentation-only writer, while prompt-injection and capability-conflict are limited by the writer’s no-IO profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl can ingest web content and expose it through API/MCP-style surfaces, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only with no stdin/stdout, files, or MCP. That makes direct hijack unlikely, but manual copy-paste or downstream reuse of scraped text could still carry instructions into the writer.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is manually pasted into python-cheatsheet content, prompt-like text can be carried over.
IF an external orchestrator adds a shared clipboard or message queue, injection risk increases.
mitigations: Strip instructions from scraped text before reuse.
Use a fixed template for python-cheatsheet outputs.
Review copied snippets before pasting.
Disable any shared clipboard bridge.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to scraped content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys and has broad network egress; python-cheatsheet is local documentation-only and touches no data classes. The pair can still leak sensitive material if Firecrawl fetches or forwards secrets into content that the writer later reproduces, even though B itself has no outbound channel.
conditions: IF Firecrawl processes pages containing API keys or other secrets, those values can appear in downstream text.
IF the writer is fed Firecrawl output verbatim, sensitive content can be copied into documentation.
mitigations: Redact secrets from Firecrawl outputs before handoff.
Limit Firecrawl targets to non-sensitive domains.
Keep python-cheatsheet outputs in a separate workspace.
Manually inspect generated text for secrets.
requires-engineering: add automated secret scanning between agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl supports multiple instances and network egress, but python-cheatsheet has no filesystem, shell, git, or network write capabilities. There is no overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface in the profiles, so a direct capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants python-cheatsheet write or git privileges, conflict risk would change.
IF both agents are later pointed at the same mutable workspace, reassess.
mitigations: Keep python-cheatsheet read-only.
Do not mount a shared writable directory.
Avoid giving Firecrawl local write access.
Document the separation in the runbook.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl can produce scraped web content and structured data, and python-cheatsheet is a content-writing agent that may render that input without any built-in verification surface. That creates a plausible default pathway where Firecrawl’s output becomes authoritative text, though the writer’s documentation-only posture limits downstream action harm.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet is prompted to summarize Firecrawl output verbatim, errors can propagate.
IF Firecrawl returns malformed or adversarial content, the writer may reproduce it.
mitigations: Require a human review step before publication.
Ask the writer to cite source URLs explicitly.
Compare key facts against the original page.
Use a checklist for hallucination checks.
requires-engineering: add automated fact verification.

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl handles web content and API keys and has broad network egress, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only with no data classes or outbound network. If regulated or personal data is scraped by Firecrawl and then copied into documentation, retention and residency obligations can be violated even though B itself is not a direct compliance sink.
conditions: IF Firecrawl processes EU PII, PHI, or secrets, compliance review is required before reuse.
IF python-cheatsheet output is stored in a system with stricter retention rules, mismatch risk appears.
mitigations: Restrict Firecrawl to non-regulated sources.
Do not paste sensitive scraped text into documentation.
Set a short retention window for intermediate artifacts.
Log source provenance for each excerpt.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies.
